questions.explanation: Weaning is the process of transitioning young animals from a milk-based diet to solid feed, marking their nutritional independence from the mother.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: Castration of male livestock is carried out mainly to
options: cure existing bacterial infections
increase the animal's fertility
reduce aggressiveness and improve meat quality by preventing unwanted breeding
improve the animal's ability to reproduce
questions.explanation: Castration removes the testes of male animals not intended for breeding, reducing aggressive behaviour and often improving growth rate and meat quality.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: According to the law of demand, when the price of a commodity rises while other factors remain constant, the quantity demanded will generally
options: rise sharply before falling
fall
remain exactly the same
rise
questions.explanation: The law of demand states that, all else being equal, an increase in the price of a commodity leads to a decrease in the quantity consumers are willing to buy.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: According to the law of supply, when the price of an agricultural commodity rises while other factors remain constant, the quantity supplied by producers will generally
options: remain unchanged
decrease
increase
fall to zero
questions.explanation: The law of supply states that, all else being equal, producers are willing to supply more of a commodity as its price rises, due to the higher potential profit.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: The law of diminishing returns in agricultural production states that as more units of a variable input (e.g., fertiliser) are added to a fixed input (e.g., land),
options: output will continue to increase at a constant rate indefinitely
the additional output gained from each extra unit will eventually decrease
total output will decrease immediately from the very first unit added
the fixed input becomes unnecessary for further production
questions.explanation: The law of diminishing returns states that, beyond a certain point, adding more of a variable input to a fixed input yields progressively smaller increases in output.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: The elasticity of demand for an agricultural product measures
options: the distance the product travels from farm to market
the total quantity of the product available in the market
how responsive the quantity demanded is to a change in the product's price
the number of farmers producing the product
questions.explanation: Elasticity of demand quantifies how much the quantity demanded of a good changes in response to a change in its price, indicating whether demand is elastic or inelastic.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: In a competitive market, the equilibrium price of a farm product is the price at which
options: supply always exceeds demand indefinitely
the government fixes prices regardless of demand or supply
demand always exceeds supply indefinitely
the quantity demanded by consumers equals the quantity supplied by producers
questions.explanation: Market equilibrium occurs where the demand and supply curves intersect, meaning the quantity buyers wish to purchase exactly matches the quantity sellers wish to offer at that price.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: Middlemen in agricultural marketing perform the important function of
options: providing veterinary services to livestock farmers
setting national agricultural policy
linking farmers with consumers by buying, transporting, and distributing produce
growing crops on behalf of the farmer
questions.explanation: Middlemen bridge the gap between producers and final consumers by assembling, transporting, storing, and distributing agricultural produce through the marketing chain.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: Grading and standardisation, as marketing functions, mainly involve
options: storing produce until prices become favourable
transporting produce from the farm to the market
sorting farm produce into uniform classes based on quality, size, or other set standards
advertising produce to potential buyers
questions.explanation: Grading sorts produce into categories based on defined quality standards (e.g., size, ripeness), helping to ensure fair pricing and consistent quality for buyers.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: Storage, as a marketing function, benefits farmers mainly by
options: allowing produce to be held until market conditions or prices become more favourable
reducing the total quantity of produce available for sale
eliminating the need for any form of transportation
guaranteeing that produce will never spoil
questions.explanation: Storage bridges the gap between harvest time and the time of sale, allowing farmers to avoid glut periods of low prices and sell when demand and prices are more favourable.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: Transportation, as a marketing function, is important mainly because it
options: determines the biological maturity of the crop
eliminates the need for storage facilities
moves agricultural produce from areas of production to areas of demand
increases the nutritional value of the produce
questions.explanation: Transportation creates place utility by physically moving produce from surplus production areas to markets or consumers where it is needed, often over considerable distances.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: The individual method of agricultural extension, such as a farm visit, is most useful mainly because it
options: requires no direct interaction between the agent and the farmer
reaches the largest possible number of farmers at the lowest cost
allows the extension agent to address a specific farmer's unique problems directly
is always cheaper than group or mass methods
questions.explanation: Individual methods, such as farm and home visits, allow the extension agent to give personalised advice tailored to a specific farmer's circumstances and problems.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: Field demonstrations are a group method of agricultural extension used mainly to
options: replace the need for individual farm visits entirely
collect taxes from farmers in a community
practically show a group of farmers how to apply a new technique or technology
broadcast general farming tips to an entire region via radio
questions.explanation: Demonstrations allow extension agents to show a group of farmers, through practical hands-on example, how an improved practice or technology works and its benefits.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: Mass methods of agricultural extension, such as radio and television broadcasts, are particularly useful mainly because they
options: can quickly reach a very large number of farmers spread over a wide area
are only effective for farmers who can read and write
provide highly personalised advice tailored to one farmer
require face-to-face interaction with every farmer reached
questions.explanation: Mass media methods can disseminate general farming information to a very large and geographically dispersed audience simultaneously, though they lack the personalised touch of individual methods.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: Farm budgeting mainly involves
options: measuring the physical size of farmland
planning expected income and expenditure for a farm business over a given period
recording only the crops harvested during a season
diagnosing diseases affecting farm animals
questions.explanation: A farm budget is a financial plan estimating anticipated income and expenses, helping the farmer allocate resources efficiently and evaluate the profitability of planned activities.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: Depreciation of farm assets, such as machinery, refers to the
options: gradual reduction in the value of an asset over time due to wear and tear or obsolescence
increase in the market value of an asset over time
amount of interest charged on a farm loan
total replacement cost of a new machine
questions.explanation: Depreciation accounts for the loss in value of a durable asset like a tractor over its useful life, due to factors such as wear, age, and obsolescence.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: Family labour differs from hired labour on a farm mainly in that family labour
options: cannot be used for any farm operations
is usually unpaid or informally compensated and provided by household members
is exclusively used on large commercial farms
always requires a formal, legally binding wage contract
questions.explanation: Family labour is typically supplied by household members without a formal wage arrangement, common on subsistence and small-scale farms, unlike hired labour which is paid a wage.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: In farm cost analysis, a fixed cost is one that
options: only applies to the cost of seeds and fertiliser
remains constant regardless of the level of output produced, such as land rent
changes directly in proportion to the level of output produced
is incurred only after the produce has been sold
questions.explanation: Fixed costs, such as rent on land or depreciation on buildings, remain constant in the short run regardless of how much is produced, unlike variable costs such as seeds or labour, which change with output.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: A rational farm manager aiming to maximise profit will generally continue production up to the point where
options: total cost is completely eliminated
the additional revenue from one more unit of output equals the additional cost of producing it
total revenue is exactly zero
all available land has been used regardless of cost
questions.explanation: Profit is maximised at the point where marginal revenue equals marginal cost; producing beyond this point would add more to cost than to revenue, reducing overall profit.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: In farm surveying, a measuring tape or chain is used mainly to
options: determine the exact chemical composition of the soil
measure the moisture content of harvested grain
measure horizontal distances between points on a farm
determine the direction of true north
questions.explanation: A measuring tape or surveyor's chain is a basic tool used to measure linear distances on the ground when carrying out a farm survey.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: A magnetic compass is used in farm surveying mainly to
options: determine directions and bearings between survey points
measure rainfall received on the farm
test the fertility of the soil
measure the exact area of a plot of land
questions.explanation: A compass determines directions and bearings, essential for accurately plotting the layout and boundaries of farmland during a survey.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: When siting a farmstead, one of the most important factors to consider is
options: the political affiliation of nearby landowners
the availability of a nearby cinema
the exact number of trees present on the site
proximity to a reliable water source and good road access
questions.explanation: A good farmstead site should have easy access to water for domestic and farm use, as well as good roads for transporting inputs and produce, among other planning considerations.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: Fencing around a farmstead or field is important mainly because it helps to
options: improve the taste of crops grown within it
keep out stray animals and unauthorised persons, protecting crops and livestock
eliminate the need for any form of irrigation
increase the fertility of the enclosed soil
questions.explanation: Fencing provides a physical barrier that protects crops and livestock from stray animals, pests, and unauthorised access, contributing to farm security.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: Human power remains an important source of farm power, especially on small-scale farms, mainly because it
options: is readily available and requires no special fuel or complex machinery
requires no rest or food to sustain the worker
can perform large-scale mechanised operations faster than a tractor
is always more efficient than animal or mechanical power
questions.explanation: Human labour remains a widely accessible power source, especially where mechanisation is limited, though it is generally slower and less efficient for large-scale operations than animal or mechanical power.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: Draught animals, such as oxen, are used on many farms as a source of power mainly for
options: producing eggs for sale
generating electricity for farm buildings
providing milk exclusively
pulling implements such as ploughs and carts
questions.explanation: Draught animals like oxen and donkeys provide animal power used to pull farm implements such as ploughs, harrows, and carts, particularly where mechanisation is limited.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: Mechanical power, supplied mainly by internal combustion engines in tractors, is valued in modern agriculture mainly because it
options: is always cheaper to acquire than animal power
requires no maintenance once purchased
performs farm operations faster and with greater capacity than human or animal power
eliminates the need for any form of fuel
questions.explanation: Mechanical power from engines allows farm operations to be completed much faster and on a larger scale than relying solely on human or animal labour, though it requires fuel and maintenance.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: Diesel engines are commonly preferred over petrol engines in farm tractors mainly because diesel engines
options: cannot generate enough power for tillage operations
run only on electricity rather than fuel
are generally more fuel-efficient and durable under heavy farm workloads
require spark plugs to ignite the fuel-air mixture
questions.explanation: Diesel engines are valued in tractors for their durability, torque, and fuel efficiency under the heavy, sustained workloads typical of farm operations, compared to petrol engines.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: Tissue culture, a biotechnology technique, is used mainly to
options: measure the pH of farm soil
control weeds using chemical herbicides
breed livestock through natural mating only
produce large numbers of genetically identical, disease-free plantlets from a small piece of plant tissue
questions.explanation: Tissue culture propagates plants by growing small explants of plant tissue in a sterile nutrient medium, rapidly producing numerous genetically identical and disease-free plantlets.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: Genetic engineering in agriculture mainly involves
options: the traditional cross-breeding of two different plant varieties
the mechanical harvesting of genetically identical crops
the physical grafting of one plant onto another
the direct manipulation of an organism's genes to introduce desirable traits
questions.explanation: Genetic engineering directly alters an organism's DNA, often by inserting specific genes, to confer desired traits such as pest resistance, faster growth, or improved nutritional content.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: Biotechnology has been applied in agriculture to develop crop varieties that are mainly
options: dependent solely on organic manure for growth
incapable of producing any seeds
unable to be consumed by humans
resistant to specific pests, diseases, or environmental stresses
questions.explanation: Modern agricultural biotechnology has produced crop varieties engineered for traits such as pest and disease resistance, herbicide tolerance, and improved drought tolerance.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: The use of Global Positioning System (GPS) technology in precision farming mainly helps farmers to
options: accurately map fields and apply inputs such as fertiliser at precise locations and rates
replace the need for any soil testing
manually water crops without any equipment
eliminate the need for farm labour entirely
questions.explanation: GPS technology enables precise mapping of field variability, allowing farmers to apply water, fertiliser, and other inputs at the right location and rate, reducing waste and improving efficiency.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: Precision farming is best described as an agricultural management approach that
options: applies a uniform, fixed amount of input across an entire farm regardless of variability
relies solely on traditional manual methods without any technology
uses technology and data to apply the right input, in the right amount, at the right place and time
focuses only on livestock production and ignores crops
questions.explanation: Precision farming uses technologies such as GPS, sensors, and data analysis to tailor input application to the specific needs of different parts of a field, improving efficiency and reducing waste.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: A seed drill, used in mechanised planting, is designed mainly to
options: remove weeds from between crop rows
place seeds at a uniform depth and spacing in rows
spray pesticides evenly over a field
harvest mature grain crops
questions.explanation: A seed drill (planter) sows seeds mechanically at a consistent depth and row spacing, improving planting uniformity and efficiency compared to manual broadcasting.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: A knapsack sprayer, commonly used on small farms, is a device designed mainly to
options: harvest root crops from the soil
apply liquid pesticides or herbicides to crops in a fine mist
irrigate large fields with a constant flow of water
till the soil before planting
questions.explanation: A knapsack sprayer is a portable, back-carried device that applies pesticides, herbicides, or foliar fertilisers to crops as a fine spray, well-suited to small-scale farming.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: A silo, as a farm structure, is used mainly for
options: processing raw milk into cheese
the storage of grains or silage in bulk
grinding grains into flour
housing livestock during the rainy season
questions.explanation: A silo is a tall, cylindrical storage structure designed to hold large quantities of grain or fermented fodder (silage), protecting it from moisture and pests.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: In farm land measurement, one hectare is equivalent to an area of
options: 10,000 square metres
1,000 square metres
100,000 square metres
100 square metres
questions.explanation: A hectare is a standard unit of land area equal to 10,000 square metres, commonly used to express the size of farms and fields.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: A theodolite is a surveying instrument used mainly to
options: test the pH level of farm soil
weigh harvested farm produce
measure the moisture content of soil samples
measure horizontal and vertical angles accurately
questions.explanation: A theodolite is a precision optical instrument used in land surveying to measure horizontal and vertical angles, essential for accurate mapping and layout of land.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: When operating farm machinery such as tractors and power tillers, it is important for the operator to observe safety precautions mainly to
options: increase the fuel consumption of the machine
reduce the working life of the machinery
prevent accidents and injuries to the operator and other farm workers
avoid the need for any form of training
questions.explanation: Following safety precautions, such as proper training, using protective gear, and following operating manuals, reduces the risk of accidents and injuries when operating farm machinery.
